# PPTX to PDF Converter

Convert PowerPoint (PPTX) documents to PDF locally using LibreOffice. Simple, fast, no cloud services required.
page_texts.2:
[.utils/formatters/pptx2pdf/README.md#features]

## Features

- **Local Conversion**: Uses LibreOffice (no internet required)
- **Batch Processing**: Convert multiple presentations at once
- **Preserves Layout**: Maintains all formatting, animations become static
- **Fast**: Direct PPTX→PDF conversion without intermediate steps
- **Standalone Portable**: Self-contained tool that can be copied to any repository
- **No Python Dependencies**: Only requires LibreOffice installation
page_texts.3:
[.utils/formatters/pptx2pdf/README.md#installation]

## Installation

All document conversion tools share a unified environment at the repository root.
page_texts.4:
[.utils/formatters/pptx2pdf/README.md#one-time-setup-from-repository-root]

### One-Time Setup (From Repository Root)

```bash
# Create virtual environment in _tools
python3 -m venv _tools/.venv

# Activate virtual environment
# Mac/Linux:
source _tools/.venv/bin/activate
# Windows:
_tools\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# Install all dependencies
pip install -r _tools/requirements.txt
```

**Prerequisites:**

- **Python 3.13+** (check with `python3 --version`)
- **LibreOffice** (required for PPTX to PDF conversion)

**Installing LibreOffice:**

**Windows (Chocolatey):**

```powershell
choco install libreoffice
```

**Mac (Homebrew):**

```bash
brew install --cask libreoffice
```

**Linux (apt):**

```bash
sudo apt install libreoffice
```

Or download from [libreoffice.org](https://www.libreoffice.org/download/download/)

**Note:** The virtual environment needs to be activated each time you open a new terminal session.

[.utils/formatters/pptx2pdf/README.md#usage]

## Usage

**Remember:** Activate the virtual environment first:

```bash
# Mac/Linux:
source _tools/.venv/bin/activate
# Windows:
_tools\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
```

All examples run from the repository root:
page_texts.6:
[.utils/formatters/pptx2pdf/README.md#convert-a-single-pptx]

### Convert a Single PPTX

```bash
# Basic conversion (output to same directory as PPTX)
python _tools/pptx2pdf/pptx2pdf.py path/to/presentation.pptx

# With verbose output
python _tools/pptx2pdf/pptx2pdf.py path/to/presentation.pptx -v

# Specify output location
python _tools/pptx2pdf/pptx2pdf.py path/to/presentation.pptx --output path/to/output.pdf
```
page_texts.7:
[.utils/formatters/pptx2pdf/README.md#convert-multiple-pptx-files]

### Convert Multiple PPTX Files

```bash
python _tools/pptx2pdf/pptx2pdf.py path/to/folder/*.pptx -v
```
page_texts.8:
[.utils/formatters/pptx2pdf/README.md#what-converts]

## What Converts

✓ **All Slide Content** - Text, images, shapes preserved
✓ **Formatting** - Fonts, colors, alignment maintained
✓ **Tables & Charts** - Rendered as they appear in PowerPoint
✓ **SmartArt** - Converted to static graphics
✓ **Embedded Images** - Included in PDF
✓ **Multi-slide Decks** - All slides in a single PDF
✓ **Animations** - Rendered in final state (not animated)
✓ **Transitions** - Not preserved (PDF is static)
page_texts.9:
[.utils/formatters/pptx2pdf/README.md#examples]

## Examples

```bash
# From repository root (with .venv activated)

# Convert a presentation
python _tools/pptx2pdf/pptx2pdf.py assets/presentations/quarterly-review.pptx -v

# Convert and specify output location
python _tools/pptx2pdf/pptx2pdf.py assets/presentations/report.pptx \
  --output docs/quarterly-report.pdf -v

# Convert all presentations in a folder
python _tools/pptx2pdf/pptx2pdf.py assets/presentations/*.pptx -v

# Quick conversion (no verbose output)
python _tools/pptx2pdf/pptx2pdf.py training-deck.pptx
```
page_texts.11:
[.utils/formatters/pptx2pdf/README.md#libreoffice-not-found]

### "LibreOffice not found"

Install LibreOffice (see Installation section above). After installation:

- **Windows**: Check if `C:\Program Files\LibreOffice\` exists
- **Mac/Linux**: Run `soffice --version` to verify
- Restart your terminal after installation
page_texts.12:
[.utils/formatters/pptx2pdf/README.md#conversion-timeout]

### Conversion Timeout

Large presentations (100+ slides) may timeout. The tool allows 60 seconds per conversion. For very large files:

- Split the presentation into smaller parts
- Convert one at a time instead of batch processing
page_texts.13:
[.utils/formatters/pptx2pdf/README.md#fonts-look-different]

### Fonts Look Different

LibreOffice uses available system fonts. If the original presentation uses custom fonts:

- Install those fonts on your system before conversion
- Or accept LibreOffice's font substitution
page_texts.15:
[.utils/formatters/pptx2pdf/README.md#combine-with-other-tools]

### Combine with Other Tools

```bash
# PowerPoint → PDF (this tool)
cd _tools/pptx2pdf
python pptx2pdf.py presentation.pptx -v

# PDF → Markdown (for AI processing)
cd ../pdf2md
python pdf2md.py ../../presentation.pdf -v
```
page_texts.16:
[.utils/formatters/pptx2pdf/README.md#batch-processing-pattern]

### Batch Processing Pattern

```bash
# Convert all PPTX files in a directory structure
find ../../assets -name "*.pptx" -exec python pptx2pdf.py {} -v \;
```

## Comparison to Cloud Services

| Feature           | pptx2pdf (Local) | Cloud Services         |
| ----------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------- |
| Internet Required | ❌ No            | ✓ Yes                  |
| File Upload       | ❌ No            | ✓ Required             |
| Privacy           | ✓ 100% Local     | ⚠️ Files sent to cloud |
| Speed             | ✓ Fast (local)   | ⚠️ Depends on network  |
| Cost              | ✓ Free           | ⚠️ Often paid          |
| Batch Processing  | ✓ Easy           | ⚠️ Limited             |
